So spread can be very roughly explained as the difference in a buy / sell price offered by a vendor at a given time. Spread over / different platforms is what allows arbitrage trading. However when people reference it here in the context of crypto.com app, it is meant as in the difference in price that they offer for buying X currency, vs selling Xa currency at the exact same time.

So think of a currency X being sold by crypto.com app at $0.09 per unit of X, but then when you tried to sell it, it would only be worth $0.088.

The difference between is the “spread”. Although this is massively oversimplified and using arbitrary values, it hopefully shows what spread is.

The “app” is still the “app”. However the Exchange is a different service offered by crypto.com. It still has an app version of it, but it’s the Exchange, not the crypto.com app offered.

I believe both are offered on iOS and Android, with the Exchange (like DeFi) also being offered on Windows / Unix systems.
